articles.title: Roadworks Scheduled for Nowell Road and Pershore Road in Middleton on 26 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on The Esplanade will commence on 4 October 2026, resulting in temporary road closures.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that roadworks on The Esplanade will begin on 4 October 2026. The works are scheduled to take place overnight, although the exact start date will be confirmed and signed on site prior to commencement.

The roadworks will involve a temporary closure of The Esplanade, starting at the junction with St Mary's Gate and extending 20 metres eastward. During this period, there will be no alternative route available for vehicles.

A marshal will be present on site to facilitate safe access to nearby car parks. Residents and motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the closure may impact local traffic flow.

For further information, including a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester, residents can visit the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Restoration of Historic Packer Spout Steps Completed in Rochdale Town Centre
articles.excerpt: The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a historic feature over 400 years old, has been completed, linking Rochdale Town Hall to St Chad’s Church.
articles.content_html:
The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a unique set of historic steps over 400 years old, has been completed in the heart of Rochdale town centre. These steps, which run through the Broadfield Park Slopes, connect the major historic attractions of Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, which has parts dating back to Saxon times.

Dating from before 1660, the Packer Spout steps have a rich history. They were traditionally used by mourning relatives who would ascend the steps to St Chad’s Church to scatter rue and rosemary in the churchyard as offerings for their loved ones. The steps are situated in the recently restored Broadfield Park Slopes area, which during the Victorian period was known for its notorious slum, referred to as 'the gank'. This area was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, and high crime rates, with many mill workers residing there.

The restoration project was undertaken by Oldham contractor Maysand, who faced significant challenges due to the steepness of the site. A special pulley system with tracks and rollers was devised to transport the stone up the hill. The team meticulously removed all 122 steps, many of which were broken and uneven, before reconstructing both the steps and the area underneath using traditional sandstone to match the existing stone.

The completion of this restoration not only preserves an important historical feature of Rochdale but also enhances the connection between key local landmarks. The Packer Spout steps are expected to attract visitors and residents alike, contributing to the cultural heritage of the town.

articles.title: First Businesses Move into Rochdale’s Sandbrook Business Park Following Strong Demand
articles.excerpt: Three lettings have been confirmed at Sandbrook Business Park in Rochdale, with BICS (NW) becoming the first occupier of the newly-completed development.
articles.content_html:
Chorley-based developer Northern Trust Company has welcomed the first businesses to its newly-completed Sandbrook Business Park in Rochdale. The company reported strong demand for the units, resulting in three lettings and several others currently under offer.

BICS (NW) has secured Unit 16D and is the first company to occupy the new development. The firm provides high voltage and low voltage electrical and engineering services across the North West, including installation, maintenance, and repairs.

Neill Burns, Director at BICS (NW), expressed satisfaction with the new premises, stating that the location is ideal for their business. He noted the modern design and high standard of the development as key factors in their decision to move in. The company currently employs seven people and views this move as crucial for their growth and expansion.

The Sandbrook Business Park is expected to attract further interest from businesses seeking modern facilities in a strategic location, contributing positively to the local economy.

articles.title: Rochdale Competes with Exeter City for Huddersfield Defender Jay Sway
articles.excerpt: Rochdale is reportedly in a transfer battle with Exeter City to secure the loan signing of Huddersfield Town's young defender Jay Sway, who has recently made his League One debut.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC is reportedly competing with Exeter City in the race to sign young defender Jay Sway on loan from Huddersfield Town. The Spotland club had previously shown interest in Sway earlier this month but faced competition from Oldham Athletic before they opted to sign Lewis Temple from Bolton Wanderers instead.

Sway, a 19-year-old full-back, made his League One debut for Huddersfield in their recent 1-1 draw against MK Dons and has also featured in the EFL Cup against Preston North End. His performances have attracted attention from several clubs, including Championship sides, leading Huddersfield to secure him on a new three-year contract after his loan spell at Hartlepool United.

Rochdale's need for a left-back is pressing, with only Bryant Bilongo available as a senior option in that position. Dan Moss has provided cover, playing the majority of the recent League Two match against Crawley Town, but the club is keen to bolster their defensive options ahead of the upcoming fixtures.

As the transfer window progresses, it remains to be seen whether Rochdale can secure Sway's services or if Exeter City will succeed in their pursuit. The outcome of this transfer battle could significantly impact Rochdale's defensive lineup as they aim to improve their performance in the league.

articles.title: Pakistan Refuses to Repatriate Rochdale Grooming Gang Leader Shabir Ahmed
articles.excerpt: Pakistan has informed UK officials, including Ed Miliband, that it will not accept the return of Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

04:15, 29 August 2026

Pakistan has informed UK officials, including Ed Miliband, that it will not accept the return of Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison.

Pakistan has officially rejected the United Kingdom's request to repatriate Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, who was released from prison on July 2, 2026. The announcement came during a meeting between Ed Miliband, the UK Labour Party leader, and Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister.

During the discussions, Dar stated that there is no bilateral agreement between the UK and Pakistan that would allow for the transfer of individuals convicted of serious crimes, such as child sexual exploitation. He emphasised that Pakistan currently lacks the legislative framework to facilitate such repatriations, stating, "We currently do not have any legislation or formal mechanism under which we can take him back."

The UK government has been under pressure to address the situation, as it continues to fund Ahmed's probation terms, which reportedly cost thousands of pounds. The diplomatic discussions have highlighted the complexities of international law regarding the repatriation of convicted criminals, particularly in cases involving serious offences.

As it stands, the UK may need to consider alternative arrangements or negotiations if it wishes to resolve the issue of Ahmed's status. The situation remains fluid, and further diplomatic efforts may be required to address the implications of Ahmed's release and the UK's ongoing responsibilities.

The decision to appoint a permanent chair follows a review aimed at providing stability and continuity in leadership for Rochdale Boroughwide Housing.

As chair, Roberts will focus on addressing housing needs in the borough and improving services for residents. Further details on his plans are expected in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Police Investigate Dog Attack on Sheep at Piethorne Reservoir, Milnrow
articles.excerpt: Police are seeking witnesses following a dog attack on sheep near Piethorne Reservoir, resulting in one sheep's death. The incident occurred on 18 August 2026.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

04:31, 29 August 2026

Police are investigating a dog attack that led to the death of a sheep near Piethorne Reservoir in Milnrow on 18 August. They are seeking information from the public.

13:41, 27 August 2026

Police are seeking witnesses following a dog attack on sheep near Piethorne Reservoir, resulting in one sheep's death. The incident occurred on 18 August 2026.

Police are appealing for witnesses after a dog attacked a group of sheep near Piethorne Reservoir in Milnrow, resulting in one sheep dying from its injuries. The incident occurred at approximately 8.45pm on 18 August 2026, according to Greater Manchester Police (GMP).

Officers have released an image of a man they wish to speak to in connection with the attack, as they believe he may have information that could assist their enquiries. GMP stated, "Officers are appealing for information regarding reports of a dog attacking sheep resulting in one of them dying."

Anyone with information is encouraged to contact GMP on 101 or via LiveChat, quoting log number 18/08/2026. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to the charity Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111.

The police investigation aims to gather more details about the incident and identify the owner of the dog involved. Local residents are urged to remain vigilant and report any similar incidents to the authorities.
